_doc: Manual-only faction lore, keyed by faction id. people: a short label for the eyebrow; tagline: the banner line; intro and plays: Markdown. Canon lives in docs/STORY.md and docs/FACTIONS.md; keep these consistent with both.

concord.tagline: A dying feudal league of scarred veterans in dented plate, holding the river roads it can no longer pay for.
concord.intro:
The Aldmere Concord was once the strongest power on the river roads: a league of lords sworn to the crown at Aldmere, far in the north, and of towns like Greyhold that hold its southern edge. A hundred years ago its knights held the gate of the Wound while five peoples sealed the Ashen Host inside. Sir Orrin Wren died there, and the Concord carved his name into every chapel wall.

The league has grown old since. Forty years ago it stopped paying the Forge for the upkeep of the Lockstone. It felled the Elderwold for timber and charcoal to feed its foundries. It did not know what either choice would cost, and in the Year of the Red Sky it learns why nobody answers when it calls.

The Concord's soldiers are not shining heroes. They are farmers with pikes, yeomen with bows and knights whose armour has been hammered straight too many times. They hold because they have always held.
concord.plays:
The Concord is the anvil: the reference combined-arms army. Braced pikes and a shield wall pin the enemy in place, longbows thin it from the back, and heavy lancers hit whatever is pinned. Lantern priests heal and steady morale, so a Concord army rarely breaks.

- **Strong:** in long fights on open grassland, and with a hero who raises morale. Every tier is priced at par, so no week is a weak week.
- **Weak:** against armies that never close, and in the cinder wastes.
- **At the top:** the Iron Sovereign strikes first, strips armour with every blow and gives every stack +2 attack. The Citadel Colossus taunts, ripostes and shields the army.

hollow.tagline: The dead of the southern fens, ruled from Sallowmere by a regent who has not died in three hundred years.
hollow.intro:
In the south lies Sallowmere: fens, grave-towns, barrows older than any crown. The dead there do not rest. They are ruled by Ysmay Vane, the Unburied Regent, who took the throne three hundred years ago and never gave it up. A hundred years ago the dead of Sallowmere marched with the living to seal the Wound. Nobody on the surface likes to remember that.

The Hollow Dominion is not evil. When the Lockstone cracks, the warm earth drives the dead up out of their barrows and north onto the living's land. They are not rising to serve the demons. They are fleeing them. A frightened army still marches, and Ysmay means to turn its terror into a kingdom.

The dead cannot be charmed, frightened or corrupted. They have no minds left to turn.
hollow.plays:
The Hollow Dominion wins by attrition. Its infantry is slow and its archers few, but it does not break: every unit is **mindless**, so morale is always zero, leadership does nothing and fear has no hold. Corpse weavers stitch fallen undead back into the line, and the upper tiers drain life and regenerate.

- **Strong:** in long battles and in the swamp, against armies that rely on fear or morale swings.
- **Weak:** on grassland, and against fire: the burned dead do not come back.
- **At the top:** the Rotwing Sovereign drains 40% of the damage it deals and costs the enemy two morale.

ashen.tagline: The fire the world was built on. A hundred years shut in the Wound starved it and broke it into broods.
ashen.intro:
In the east, past the last towns, a ring of black rock surrounds a burning chasm: the Wound. Every few centuries the Ashen Host climbs out of it and is driven back, never shut in, until the Sealing a hundred years ago. Since then the Host has starved in the dark and broken into broods that eat each other.

Skarn Ashborn was a pit-chief with nothing. When the Lockstone begins to crack, he climbs out of the Gnawing Pit, unites the broods by force and leads them up to burn everyone who shut them in. His demons are monstrous and distinctly inhuman: slag-spawn, skinless hounds, hook-armed flayers and burning titans. They want out. That is all they have ever wanted.
ashen.plays:
The Ashen Host is the hammer that has to win before it runs out of bodies. Its creatures are fast, fragile and aggressive; many cannot be answered back (relentless) or set wounds burning. It has only one true ranged unit.

- **Strong:** in the first two weeks. Low tiers are cheap and grow fast, and the cinder wastes favour it.
- **Weak:** on snow, and in long wars against factions whose top tiers outclass its own.
- **At the top:** the Maw of Ruin swallows two stacks at once, heals on what it devours and terrifies. The Pyre Sovereign rises again from its ashes.

thornwood.tagline: The keepers of the Elderwold, who knew what its roots were holding and let the axes come anyway.
thornwood.intro:
West of Greyhold stood the Elderwold, the oldest forest in the world. Its Heartroots reached down into the Wound and gripped the Lockstone when the Sealing was made. The Thornwood Covenant, gaunt bark-skinned hunters and druids, has kept that wood for longer than it has had a name.

For forty years the Covenant has watched Concord foresters cut the Elderwold to stumps. Only the Last Grove still stands. When Cerrid Ashbark goes to war for it, he learns what his own druids kept quiet: they knew what the roots were for, and they said nothing.
thornwood.plays:
The Thornwood is a fortress of bows. Four of its eight tiers shoot, behind regenerating wardens and taunting ancients. It has one flyer and **no cavalry** at all.

- **Strong:** in the forest, and whenever its front line holds long enough for the volleys to land.
- **Weak:** when cavalry or flyers reach the back line, and in the cinder wastes.
- **At the top:** the Wyrdthorn Matriarch fires two volleys a turn, each able to pin its target in thorns.

forge.tagline: The smith-clans under the western mountains. They cast the Lockstone, were never paid, and shut their gates.
forge.intro:
Under the mountain spine in the west live the smith-clans of the Sunken Forge, soot-black deep folk who work iron, rune and steam. A hundred years ago the Forge cast the Lockstone that holds the Wound shut. The Concord promised to pay for its upkeep. Forty years ago it stopped.

So the Forge shut its gates and let the world outside fend for itself. Behind the gates, Runesmith Gunnra Sootmantle is the only one who believes the rock will not keep the fire out. When dead Forgemen start climbing the shafts and the stone grows warm, she learns that a mountain is not a wall.
forge.plays:
The Forge starts slow and finishes unstoppable. Its low tiers are expensive and only average; its top three tiers are the best value in the game but need ore and three rare resources. It fields slow armoured infantry, crossbows, golems, clockwork boar cavalry and a siege bombard, and **no flyers**.

- **Strong:** from week three on, on rocky highland, and in sieges.
- **Weak:** in the first two weeks, and in the swamp.
- **At the top:** the Worldforge Engine's blows hit two stacks, strip armour and ignore part of what is left.

frostmarch.tagline: The clans of the frozen north. A hundred years ago they carried their winter into the Wound. This year the ash stole their summer.
frostmarch.intro:
North of everything, under the Ancient Glacier, the Frostmarch Clans live by the axe and the long hall. They are fur-cloaked raiders, berserkers and riders of shaggy war-beasts. A hundred years ago the clans marched their winter into the Wound to bank its fire, and the song of the Sealing has a last verse that no one sings any more.

In the Year of the Red Sky, ash blots out the northern sun and the summer never comes. Ulvra Kettleborn unites the clans by the axe and leads them south for bread. The south remembers them only as raiders. They remember who was cold first.
frostmarch.plays:
The Frostmarch rushes. Nearly everything costs gold only and grows fast. It has cheap, numerous infantry, three cavalry tiers, giants and a wyrm, but **no archers and no flyers**: only the frost shaman strikes from range.

- **Strong:** in week one, on snow, and with numbers. A Frostmarch player starts a standard game with **two heroes**.
- **Weak:** in long wars against late factions, and in the cinder wastes.
- **At the top:** the Ancient Winter Wyrm's freezing breath engulfs two stacks, stuns and frightens.

darkelf.tagline: The wardens of the Nightgate, who stayed below for a thousand years because that was the duty.
darkelf.intro:
Deeper than the Forge's galleries, deeper than the Host's tunnels, lie the caverns of the Umbral Court. Before the surface peoples had names, the Court bound the dragon Karzhaloth under the world and cut out its six eyes. The Eyes became the Gate-Eyes: one was given to each surface people, so that no single hand could ever open the Nightgate again. Then the Court withdrew below.

The Court is severe, aristocratic and ruled by houses. One of them, House Vexmire, "the house that remembers the sky", was declared extinct long ago. It is not a house. It is a vow, and it has members in every house.

The Umbral Court is an expansion people. Its campaign, *The Six Eyes*, is set the year after the Red Sky.
darkelf.plays:
The Umbral Court strikes first and breaks easily. Its creatures have fewer hit points and more attack and initiative than most: swift assassins, crossbows, cave riders and dragons, backed by veil magic.

- **Strong:** on rocky highland and underground, and when it chooses where the fight happens.
- **Weak:** on open grassland, and in drawn-out battles.

fishmen.tagline: What the drowned city of Sarranth became: armoured, patient and forgetful, keeping vaults it cannot read.
fishmen.intro:
Four hundred years ago, in the Second Burning, Sarranth, the most learned city of the coast, fled into the sea behind a breathing-spell. A northern shaman, Skadric Whalebone, changed one rune of it out of envy. Sarranth's people survived as the Shoal: fish-folk, strong, long-lived and slow of mind. The surface forgot them.

The Shoal keeps the drowned city's vaults without being able to read them, until one of them can. Ilo learns what his people were and who made them what they are, and drags the Shoal onto the mainland to take its revenge on the north.

The Abyssal Shoal is an expansion people. Its campaign, *The Drowned Oath*, is set the year after the Red Sky.
fishmen.plays:
The Abyssal Shoal outlasts. Its creatures have more hit points and armour and less attack and initiative than most: shell-armoured troops, harpoons, sea beasts and tide magic.

- **Strong:** in the swamp and on the coast, in long fights.
- **Weak:** in the cold. On snow a Shoal army loses part of every stack each day unless its hero wears the Forgewarm Harness.
